item.title: It is rare to seek aircraft for accused fugitive: Chief Prosecutor
item.description:
International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam has described the wish of Sheikh Hasina, who has been sentenced to death for crimes against humanity, to return to Bangladesh on 16 December as a delusion.

On this matter, he said that it was rare in the world for someone to request an aircraft on behalf of a fugitive accused.

The chief prosecutor made these remarks in response to questions from journalists at the ICT today, Tuesday.

Deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina wants to return to Bangladesh on 16 December, Victory Day. She has called on the government to arrange for her return from Delhi, India, on an aircraft of Biman Bangladesh Airlines, the state-owned flag carrier. Sheikh Hasina’s spokesperson informed the Reuters news agency of this today, Tuesday.

Asked about the matter, Aminul Islam said, “This is a ridiculous incident. The issue of requesting an aircraft—the spokesperson who made this demand—is nothing more than a delusion on his part. The reason is that it is rare in the world for someone to request an aircraft on behalf of a fugitive accused. Therefore, such a demand cannot be accepted under any circumstances.”

A journalist asked whether the Bangladesh government had failed in its responsibility when people who were declared fugitives by the tribunal and are being tried in absentia were holding press conferences in Delhi and coming to the Bangladesh border areas, including Agartala and Petrapole.

In response, the chief prosecutor said, “They are not doing anything inside Bangladesh’s territory. Now, their activities are being seen in other countries through various media outlets. They are effectively proving to the world that the Awami League, whose activities are banned, is a terrorist party, and that its members are criminals and murderers.”

Saying that all-out efforts were under way to bring back the accused, Aminul Islam said, “We want to send a clear message. If, through their activities, they prove that the Bangladesh Awami League is a terrorist organisation, then the government and the tribunal may be compelled to take action against the organisation through the judicial process.”

item.title: 4 of a family killed in Rangpur: DB to submit chargesheet by 30 Nov
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of police will submit a chargesheet to the court by 30 November in connection with the murder of four members of a family, including retired Rangpur Zilla School teacher Ganapati Chakraborty.

The DB claims that its investigation has found evidence of the involvement of two accused in the killings, with no evidence of anyone else's involvement.

Sanatan Chakraborty, deputy commissioner of the Rangpur Police DB and the supervising officer in the case, shared the information with Prothom Alo on Tuesday morning.

Confirming that the two accused, Siddhartha Das and Mugdha Das, are currently in prison, Sanatan Chakraborty said, "Analysis of the DNA test reports and an extensive investigation have established beyond reasonable doubt their involvement in the murders."

He added that investigators had recorded statements from at least 50 people in connection with the case.

The police official said, "The chargesheet is being submitted within approximately three months of the case being transferred to the DB. Before submitting it to the court, we have to review various aspects of the investigation and carry out the necessary checks and verification. The court police also play a role in this process. We will submit the chargesheet by 30 November after completing these procedures."

DNA of two accused found in samples

Following the murders, investigators collected various samples from the crime scene and sent them to the forensic laboratory of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) in Dhaka for examination.

The DB claims that the DNA of the two accused was found in several of the samples.

Jinnat Ali, the DB inspector investigating the case, said that investigators identified Mugdha Das's DNA in a date seed sample, Siddhartha Das's DNA in a piece of cucumber, and DNA belonging to both men on a cigarette butt.

In addition, investigators found only Mugdha Das' DNA in a sample taken from the towel wrapped around the neck of victim Pritilata Chakraborty.

Investigators collected 31 types of samples from the crime scene in two phases and sent them to the CID forensic laboratory for examination.

These included date seeds, pieces of cucumber, a fruit-cutting knife, foil used for consuming yaba, cigarette butts, stains from a washbasin and blood samples from the two accused.

Jinnat Ali said, "The DNA test reports were not the only evidence. Analysis of the recovered evidence, the confessional statements of the two arrested men and witnesses' accounts has also established the involvement of Siddhartha Das and Mugdha Das. The chargesheet against them is being submitted on the basis of this evidence."

Questions were raised over whether the two female members of the family had been raped before the murders. However, the investigating officer said that DNA tests had found no evidence of rape.

Murders committed with the intention of theft

According to Jinnat Ali, the accused had learnt that Ganapati Chakraborty had withdrawn Tk 50–60 lakh from a bank after his retirement and kept the money at home. They also believed that the house contained gold jewellery.

"Their main motive was theft. They entered the house through the roof of a neighbouring building and killed the four family members one after another," he said.

On the night of 22 August this year, police recovered the bodies of Ganapati Chakraborty, his wife Pritilata Chakraborty and their two children, Agami Chakraborty and Ayush Chakraborty, from their home in Machhuapara, Rangpur city.

On 23 August, Ganapati's elder brother, Gopinath Chakraborty, filed a murder case against unidentified suspects at Kotwali police station.

Initially, the investigation was assigned to Milon Chatterjee, an inspector (investigation) at Kotwali police station.

The following day, 24 August, the Rangpur police's detective branch took charge of the investigation. DB Inspector Jinnat Ali has been investigating the case since then.

item.title: Sweden Aslam ‘used to run Dhaka’s criminal underworld’ from Malaysia
item.description:
After spending 27 and a half years in prison, Sheikh Mohammad Aslam, also known as ‘Sweden Aslam’, a top criminal on the police list, was released on 3 September 2024. After spending around two years outside prison, he has been arrested again.

Police say Aslam is accused of becoming involved in various criminal activities again, including extortion and grabbing shopping malls in the capital’s Karwan Bazar, Tejgaon and Farmgate areas. The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) had been looking for him.

Aslam was arrested from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on Sunday night. Police say he was travelling to Malaysia via Thailand on a Thai Airways flight.

Following the July 2024 mass uprising, seven notorious criminals were released on bail amid the unstable situation. Aslam was one of them. A DB source said that at one point after his release on bail, he went abroad. From there, he used to control the criminal underworld in the Karwan Bazar, Tejgaon and Farmgate areas. He would occasionally visit Dhaka.

Aslam most recently arrived in Dhaka from Malaysia on 4 November. After receiving information about his return to the country, detectives informed immigration police. A letter was sent requesting his arrest in connection with an old case, along with the relevant case documents. On the basis of that letter, he was arrested on Sunday night.

From school football star to ‘Sweden Aslam’: How he rose in Dhaka’s underworld

Ziauddin Ahmed, deputy commissioner of the DB’s Tejgaon division, told Prothom Alo yesterday, Monday, that allegations had emerged of Sweden Aslam’s renewed involvement in various crimes centred around Karwan Bazar, Tejgaon and Farmgate. He was arrested as a suspect in the Titon murder case.

At around 7:45 pm on 28 April, miscreants shot and killed Titon under a banyan tree in front of Shah Nawaz Hall of Dhaka University, on the western side of New Market in Dhaka.

He was the brother-in-law of another top criminal on the police list, Sanjidul Islam Emon. Titon’s brother, Saeed Akhtar Ripon, filed a case over the incident at New Market Police Station.

The names of several people were mentioned as suspects in the list of accused in the case. They are top criminals Imam-ul Hasan Helal, also known as Pichchi Helal; Badal, also known as Killer Badal; Shahjahan; and Rony, also known as Daggery Rony. Police have now shown Sweden Aslam as arrested in this case.

Travelled abroad 4 times in 5 months

Sources involved in the investigation said that, after analysing immigration police and passport records, they found that Aslam first travelled from Dhaka to Malaysia via Thailand on 6 April after being released on bail. He subsequently travelled between Malaysia and Dhaka three more times in August and November. A DB source said Aslam mainly lived in Malaysia, but also travelled to Thailand and Singapore.

‘Top terror’ Sweden Aslam arrested at airport

A police source said Aslam had visited the country once in August. After receiving the information, a DB team conducted a raid in the Tejgaon area. However, he managed to escape right in front of the detectives.

An official involved in the investigation told Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity that he had an old photograph of Aslam, which no longer resembled his current appearance.

During the raid, Aslam walked right past him. He saw him and asked his name but failed to recognise him. The official said that when asked his name at the time, Aslam had identified himself as Ali Akbar. After his arrest, it became clear that the person who had introduced himself as Ali Akbar was actually Aslam.

After being released on bail in 2024, Aslam became the president of a three-storey shopping complex called Capital Baro Bazar, behind Farmgate’s Ananda Cinema Hall. It is learnt that the shopping complex is now under his control. Businesspeople allege that they have to pay him extortion money to run their businesses there.

Sources involved in the investigation say Aslam’s name has also resurfaced in connection with extortion and land grabbing in Karwan Bazar. There are allegations that his associates are involved in various crimes in the area.

After 8 pm on 7 January, Swachchhasebak Dal leader Azizur Rahman, also known as Musabbir (44), was shot dead in an alley beside Hotel Super Star in West Tejturi Para. Investigators have found information suggesting that a ‘criminal’ named Dilip, also known as Binash, was involved in the murder. He is close to Aslam.

During preliminary interrogation after his arrest, Aslam denied allegations of involvement in the murder of Swachchhasebak Dal leader Musabbir. Sources said he told police that he did not know anyone named Binash. He also denied allegations that he controlled criminal activities in the Karwan Bazar, Tejgaon and Farmgate areas. He claimed that many local people approached him when they were in trouble and that he tried to resolve their problems.

In the criminal underworld since the 1980s

Sweden Aslam’s ancestral home is in Nawabganj, Dhaka. After independence, his father, Sheikh Jinnat Ali, and uncles began living on Indira Road in Dhaka. His father ran a rod and cement business in Farmgate. Aslam studied at Tejgaon Polytechnic School, now known as Tejgaon Government High School.

According to police and local sources, Aslam was a good football player as a child. He also played for his school in inter-district competitions. After passing the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination, he enrolled at a college in the Tejgaon area. It was around this time that he became involved in crime.

A report published in Prothom Alo on 23 October 2015 said Aslam was accused of shooting Shakil, a boy who was standing beside his mother in front of a school in East Rajabazar, Farmgate, in 1986. Subsequently, allegations emerged that he was involved in one murder after another.

During the 1980s and 1990s, criminal networks emerged in different parts of the capital, each under the control of a particular individual. On 27 December 2001, during the tenure of the then four-party alliance government, police published a list of 23 top criminals.

The list included criminals from different areas, such as Kala Jahangir, Subrata Bain, Pichchi Hannan and Haris Ahmed. Aslam’s name was not on that list. However, his name appeared on a list of 42 top criminals prepared by police in 2010.

Aslam’s first wife, Iti, was from Sweden. At one point, Aslam also went there. He returned to the country a few years later. Subsequently, Sheikh Aslam of Rajabazar became known as Sweden Aslam. This name was also used in police lists and case documents.

His marriage to Iti did not last. After their divorce, Iti returned to the country and married a man named Abdullah Al Hasan, also known as Mamun. In 1995, Mamun and two others were murdered in Old Dhaka. Aslam’s name appeared in the charge sheet in that case. Newspaper reports at the time said Aslam had killed Mamun because he could not accept Mamun’s romantic relationship and marriage with Iti. Later, Aslam married his paternal cousin, Simi.

The exact number of cases filed against Aslam is not known. At the time of his release in September 2024, a Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS) report mentioned 22 cases, including nine murder cases. Earlier, a Prothom Alo report in 2015, citing a letter from Dhaka Metropolitan Police, said Aslam had been acquitted in 11 of the 12 cases against him. One case was pending trial.

That case concerned the murder of Tejgaon Jubo League leader Galib. Galib was murdered on 23 March 1997. A case was filed against 20 people, including Aslam, over the incident. Police submitted the charge sheet on 8 April 1998. Aslam had not been granted bail in this case.

Aslam spent a long time at Kashimpur High Security Central Jail in Gazipur. There were also allegations that he controlled the criminal underworld while in prison. In March 2014, a team from the Department of Prisons conducted a raid and recovered two mobile phones from him.

Sources concerned with the matter said an intelligence agency had tapped those phones and obtained important information. Later, a confidential report, along with a list of calls, was sent to Dhaka Metropolitan Police. It mentioned that several criminals from East Rajabazar were working for him.

There was little progress in recording witness testimony in the Galib murder case for a long time. Galib’s wife, Shampa, testified on 15 October 2003, and Chunnu Mia testified on 24 September 2006. After that, the prosecution failed to produce any further witnesses for nine consecutive years. By the time Aslam was released on bail in 2024, testimony had been recorded from 14 of the 24 witnesses.

The bail order reached Kashimpur Jail on 3 September that year. After verification, he was released at around 9:00 pm. He was then 62 years old. He has now turned 65.

Among the seven notorious criminals released on bail amid the unstable situation following the July 2024 mass uprising were Mohammadpur-based Imam-ul Hasan Helal, also known as Pichchi Helal; Hazaribagh-based Sanjidul Islam, also known as Emon; and Mirpur-based Abbas Ali, also known as ‘Killer Abbas’. They have not been arrested. They, too, face allegations of becoming involved in criminal activities again.

item.title: Shama: Hasina to be arrested if she visits any Bangladesh mission in India
item.description:
Sheikh Hasina will be arrested if she visits any Bangladesh diplomatic mission in India, including the one in New Delhi, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam has said.
She made the comment while responding to questions from journalists at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday.
Shama Obaed said all 84 Bangladesh diplomatic missions worldwide are considered part of the country's territory. Anyone visiting these missions while abroad would therefore be arrested there, she added.
She said diplomatic efforts were underway to bring back convicted fugitives and those accused of ordering killings during the July-August uprising from India and other countries under extradition agreements.
Dismissing reports of Hasina's possible return on December 16 as “political stunts”, the state minister said she would be arrested and sent to prison if she returned. The law would take its own course, she added.
She also said Bangladesh was in regular contact with the Indian government through diplomatic channels to bring back those involved in the July-August killings, enforced disappearances and bloodshed, including the killer of Osman Hadi and those who ordered the killings.
Shama Obaed described reports of a possible return as an attempt to put ordinary Awami League leaders and activists at risk, saying efforts to create instability after abandoning party workers were pointless.

item.title: 'Awami terrorists' trying to create atmosphere of fear, govt tells diplomats
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Tuesday briefed the diplomats on the current political situation and recent security challenges and sought the international community’s support for a peaceful, stable and prosperous Bangladesh.
"We count on your continued support as we advance our democratic transition, institutional reforms and economic recovery towards a peaceful, stable and prosperous Bangladesh," he told the diplomats during a briefing at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Kobir said the recent incidents of violence and sabotage run counter to the aspirations of the people of Bangladesh, who seek peace, stability, democratic freedoms, economic opportunity and a better future.
The government remains firmly committed to meeting these aspirations and creating an enabling environment for investment, growth and development, he said.
"In this endeavour, we greatly value the understanding and constructive engagement of our international friends and partners," said the state minister.
"This briefing is taking place in the backdrop of recent violence and continued disruptive activities of the Awami terrorists," Kobir said.
No one asked any questions during the briefing, a diplomat told UNB.
Kobir said Awami terrorists are also active abroad. "They are spreading disharmony in some countries, and involved in terrorism and money laundering. We want to bring them back. We seek your cooperation in this regard."
Kobir said these incidents in the country as well as abroad are not isolated acts of political protest.
"Awami terrorists are trying to create an atmosphere of fear and insecurity among people, and provoking confrontations with law enforcement agencies to generate an impression of political disorder," he said.
By attacking police installations and attempting to loot weapons, they want to challenge the authority of the State and the rule of law, the State Minister said.
The government remains firmly committed to ensuring that these incidents do not derail Bangladesh’s democratic transition, he said.
"Law enforcement agencies have been directed to respond firmly, professionally and proportionately," he said, noting that cases have been filed, investigations are underway and those involved in unlawful acts are being held accountable in accordance with the law.
In the election, he said, Bangladesh Nationalist Party - BNP - secured a decisive electoral victory and formed the government under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
The new government assumed office amid significant challenges, he said, noting that its immediate priorities were to strengthen democratic institutions, re-establish law and order, restore public confidence, uphold the rule of law across all spheres of national life.
The government said economic recovery was another immediate priority.
"We have recently witnessed a disturbing pattern of violence, sabotage and organized disruptive activities, particularly involving terrorists associated with the Awami League and its affiliated organizations," Kobir said.
He said the activities of the Awami League and its affiliated organizations were banned under the Anti-Terrorism Act and its party registration remains suspended.
Nevertheless, Kobir said its activists have continued to organise occasional processions, blockades, demonstrations and other subversive activities in different parts of the country.
"The situation has become particularly concerning in this November," he said noting that between 1st and 21st November, a total of 158 incidents were recorded across 41 administrative units.
"These went well beyond political demonstrations – there were crude-bomb explosions, petrol-bomb attacks, arson, vandalism, looting, assaults on police installations and blockades of major highways," Kobir said.
On 17 November, a police station was attacked in Gopalganj, the birthplace of former prime minister.
The perpetrators set fire to police vehicles and the station building, looted arms and ammunition, and freed detainees from custody, seriously injuring a Border Guard Bangladesh member.
On 19 November, another police station was attacked in Muksudpur, with vehicles set ablaze and residence of the officer-in-charge damaged.
The residences of elected MPs, BNP offices and several Grameen Bank branches were also vandalised or set on fire, he said.
In Shariatpur, crude-bomb explosions and road blockades disrupted traffic and toll collection near the Padma Bridge southern toll plaza.
A bus driver was killed when a parked bus was set on fire in Faridpur.
Two BNP-affiliated local political leaders lost their lives in an attack on a procession.
In Pabna, violent clashes, arson and attacks on public property further aggravated the situation.
Reports also document attacks on police in Chittagong, crude-bomb explosions and bus arson in Dhaka, attacks on police vehicles in Sylhet and an attack on a Grameen Bank office in Noakhali.
"Labour unrest in the RMG sector is purposefully designed by the Awami League and its activists to put our economy into challenges and workers to suffer," said the State Minister.
"Between November 7 and 19, 83 transport vehicles were set on fire, crude-bomb explosions were reported at 87 locations and 72 Grameen Bank branches or offices were attacked or targeted. Four police installations were subjected to arson or vandalism. Law enforcement agencies filed 39 cases and made 66 arrests during this period," he added.
Kobir said no political affiliation justifies arson or attacks on law enforcement personnel, destruction of public property or attempts to seize weapons.
"And there cannot be any immunity for such unlawful acts. The government will not tolerate retaliatory violence or vigilantism, irrespective of the political identity of those involved," he said.

item.title: Rumour of garment worker’s death sparks protest, road blockade in Gazipur
item.description:
Police fired tear gas and sound grenades to disperse garment workers who blocked a road in Gazipur's Konabari area on Tuesday following rumours that a worker had died.
The incident sparked protests and disrupted factory operations, leaving the area tense after the workers were dispersed.
The unrest began on Tuesday morning after reports spread that a worker at Islam Garments had died. Workers from Islam Garments and Ripon Garments refused to join work and gathered near their factories.
They later took to a regional road with sticks and blocked it, prompting authorities to declare a general holiday at the two factories and several nearby establishments.
According to police and workers, officers tried to persuade the protesters to leave the road at around 9:45am. As the workers became agitated, police fired tear gas and sound grenades to bring the situation under control.
Konabari Police Station Officer-in-Charge Iftekhar Hossain said the workers had attempted to block the road and were dispersed by police.

item.title: State minister: No criminal will be allowed to return without extradition
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir has said that no criminal will ever be allowed to return to Bangladesh without going through the extradition process.
He made the remarks on Tuesday while responding to a question about ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s possible return to Bangladesh in December, after briefing foreign diplomats at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Referring to a Reuters report on Hasina’s plan to return in December, Humaiun Kobir said: “Anyone can spend money out of frustration and hire people to write many things. But aspirations and reality are two different things, and we must distinguish between them. The reality is that no criminal will ever be allowed to return to the country without going through the extradition process.”
He said someone could imagine, even in a dream or nightmare, that they could simply walk or fly back to Bangladesh. “But no, she is not an ordinary passenger. She can only be brought back to the country in handcuffs or under strict security. That is the reality,” he added.
Asked about the government's position, the state minister said it was confident because it had been elected with overwhelming public support and more than a two-thirds majority.
“This is not an arbitrary or temporary government. It has a very strong position among the people. We are therefore dealing with the situation with confidence, keeping the public's trust in mind,” he said.
Humaiun Kobir also alleged that Awami League activists were carrying out isolated acts of violence in an attempt to spread fear among people. However, he claimed that people were not afraid and that those involved in the violence were now fearful themselves.
The state minister said the Awami League had become irrelevant to the people of Bangladesh, alleging that the party had no public support and was widely disliked.
He said people wanted qualitative changes in governance following the mass uprising of August 5 and no longer wanted to see such activities. He also claimed that members of the public would hand over those involved in violence to law enforcement agencies.

item.title: Brahmanbaria residents block railway lines over proposed new upazila
item.description:
Residents of 10 villages in Machihata Union of Brahmanbaria Sadar upazila blocked the Dhaka-Chittagong and Dhaka-Sylhet railway lines for about an hour on Tuesday, protesting a proposed new upazila named Barisal.
Hundreds of people gathered near Chandpur Bazar between 11am and noon, disrupting train services on both routes.
Before the blockade, residents from different walks of life held a protest meeting at Chandpur Tamizuddin Secondary School. Participants came from several villages, including Atla, Paghachang, Chinair, Chapuir, Khewai and Phulbaria.
The meeting was chaired by Abu Sayeed Khandaker, president of the Machihata Union BNP unit. Speakers included Nurul Huda Sarkar, the district BNP's secretary for training affairs; Jahangir Alam, general secretary of the union BNP unit; and Ashikur Rahman Bhuiyan, a prospective Union Parishad chairman candidate, along with other local leaders.
After the meeting, a group of protesters moved to the nearby railway tracks and began the blockade.
The Dhaka-bound Mahanagar Express, travelling from Dhaka to Chittagong, was held up for around 20 minutes near Paghachang station. The Sylhet-bound Kalni Express, travelling from Sylhet to Dhaka, was also stopped for approximately 30 minutes.
Speaking at the protest, Nurul Huda Sarkar said there was a proposal to form a new upazila named Barisal by incorporating parts of Machihata and Basudeb unions, the newly formed Barisal Union in Brahmanbaria Sadar upazila, and Singarbil Union in Bijoynagar upazila.
He said they strongly opposed the proposal and would not allow existing Union Parishads to be dismantled to form a new upazila.
Jahangir Alam said residents had long identified themselves as people of Machihata Union and wanted to remain under the existing union. He warned that the movement would be intensified if their demands were not met.
Other protesters echoed the demand, saying they wanted to remain part of Brahmanbaria Sadar upazila and did not want to be included in a new upazila.
On receiving news of the blockade, police led by Khairul Alam, officer-in-charge of Sadar Model police station, reached the scene. Members of the Railway Police and the Railway Security Force from Akhaura also arrived.
Law enforcement personnel subsequently cleared the tracks, and train services returned to normal around noon.

item.title: DB seeks fresh seven-day remand for ex-DSCC mayor Khokon
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of police has sought a fresh seven-day remand for former Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) mayor Sayeed Khokon in a murder case over the death of teenager Abdul Motaleb during the July uprising in the capital's Dhanmondi area.
Inspector Sujan Haque of the DB's Ramna zonal team, the investigation officer in the case, filed the remand petition on Tuesday, citing five reasons for further interrogation.
State lawyer Harun-or-Rashid confirmed the matter, saying a hearing on the petition was scheduled at the Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Court in the afternoon.
The five grounds cited by investigators are:
Khokon was detained from a house in Baridhara on November 17 and handed over to the DB by the Special Response Battalion (SRB). A court granted seven days of remand the same day.
According to the case statement, Motaleb was shot dead on August 4, 2024, while taking part in a procession near Jigatala bus stand during the July uprising.
After the fall of the Awami League government, his father, Abdul Matin, filed a murder case with Dhanmondi Police Station on August 26, 2024. The case names 176 people, including former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal and former road transport and bridges minister Obaidul Quader. Khokon's name is also included among the accused.
Khokon, son of former undivided Dhaka City Corporation mayor Mohammad Hanif, was elected DSCC mayor in 2015. He did not receive the Awami League nomination for the next mayoral election but was later elected MP from Dhaka-6 in the 12th parliamentary election on the party's ticket.

item.title: Shama: Hasina’s return announcement ‘political stunt’
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam has said diplomatic efforts are under way to bring back convicted fugitives and those accused of ordering killings during the July-August uprising under extradition arrangements.
She made the remarks while responding to questions from reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday.
Dismissing reports that Sheikh Hasina might return to Bangladesh on December 16 or 17 as “political stunt”, Shama said the former prime minister would be arrested and sent to jail if she returned, and that the law would take its own course.
She said no one knew the whereabouts or plans of the former prime minister since she fled the country, adding that these were not relevant to the government's efforts to secure the return of those accused of crimes.
The state minister said Bangladesh maintained regular diplomatic communication with the Indian government to bring back those involved in killings, enforced disappearances and bloodshed during the July-August period, including the alleged killers of Sharif Osman Hadi and those accused of ordering the violence.
Regarding speculation about Hasina's possible return in December, Shama said such publicity was nothing more than an attempt to put ordinary Awami League leaders and activists at risk. She said it was pointless for Hasina, having left her party's leaders and activists behind, to attempt to create instability or unrest in Bangladesh.
She added that the positions of the foreign and law ministries on the matter were clear.
Asked whether Hasina could renew or apply for a passport or national identity card (NID), Shama referred to constitutional provisions, saying the government was not obliged to issue passports, NIDs or other documents to anyone convicted and sentenced for crimes against humanity. She said the government would not deviate from those provisions.
On the legal jurisdiction of Bangladesh's diplomatic missions abroad, the state minister said the country's 84 missions were considered part of its territory. She added that if the person concerned visited any of those missions abroad, she would be arrested there.

item.title: Chief prosecutor: Hasina’s request for aircraft to return to Bangladesh nothing but madness
item.description:
Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam has described ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s request for an aircraft to bring her back to Bangladesh as “nothing but madness”.
“Sending an aircraft to bring a death-row convict back to the country would be unprecedented. Sheikh Hasina’s request for an aircraft is nothing but madness,” he said.
He made the comments while responding to questions from journalists at his office at the International Crimes Tribunal on Tuesday.
On the prosecution's position in the case against Ziaul Ahsan, Aminul Islam said: “Criminals against humanity like Ziaul Ahsan are rare in world history. The prosecution seeks the death penalty for him, along with the confiscation of all his property.”
Regarding the progress of the trial of the Awami League as a political party, the chief prosecutor said the investigation into the party's alleged role as a terrorist organisation was ongoing.
He added that the activities of its fugitive leaders were making the party's members' alleged involvement in terrorism and killings increasingly clear.
Hasina, who has been living in exile in India for more than two years, wants to return to Bangladesh on December 16, Victory Day, reports Reuters.
Her spokesperson told the British news agency on Tuesday that she had asked the government to arrange an aircraft operated by state-owned Biman Bangladesh Airlines to bring her home.

item.title: Six members of ‘Four-Star Group’ arrested in Mirpur
item.description:
Six members of the alleged "Four-Star Group" criminal gang have been arrested in Mirpur with firearms, ammunition, locally made weapons and narcotics.
The arrests were made during a special operation conducted by Special Response Battalion (SRB)-4 on Monday night, the force said in a statement on Tuesday morning.
SRB-4 said foreign-made pistols, ammunition, a large quantity of locally made weapons and narcotics were recovered during the operation.
The force said further details would be disclosed later.

item.title: 10 injured in clash during Awami League procession in Gopalganj
item.description:
Ten people were injured in a clash between two groups during an Awami League procession in Kotalipara upazila of Gopalganj on Monday evening. Five shops were also vandalized during the incident in South Hiron village.
The procession was organised despite the ban on the Awami League's activities.
Three of the injured — Mikail Islam, 52, Mashiur Rahman, 42, and Zayed Sheikh, 36 — were admitted to Kotalipara Upazila Health Complex. As Mikail's condition deteriorated, he was transferred to Gopalganj Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment.
According to local sources, members and activists of the Awami League, Jubo League and the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League took part in the procession on Monday evening.
When the procession reached South Hiron village, an argument broke out between Mashiur Rahman, a Jubo League leader and prospective chairman candidate in the upcoming Hiron Union Parishad election, and Shafiqul Islam, brother of another prospective candidate, Munshi Raich Uddin.
The argument escalated into a clash, leaving 10 people injured and five shops vandalized.
Mashiur Rahman said the group had gone to South Hiron village as part of the procession when Shafiqul Islam and his associates attacked them, injuring several people, including himself.
Mashiur also alleged that Shafiqul's brother, Munshi Raisuddin, was involved with Jamaat-e-Islami.
Denying the allegation, Shafiqul said his elder brother lived abroad and was not involved in politics. He acknowledged his own longstanding association with the Chhatra League and alleged that he was attacked first because of rivalry over the upcoming Union Parishad election.
Shafiqul claimed that several people from his side, including himself, were injured and that five of their shops were vandalized and looted.
Kotalipara police station Officer-in-Charge Nayan Chandra Debnath said he was aware of the clash but had received no written complaint from either side.
He said police would investigate the incident and take appropriate legal action if a complaint was filed.

item.title: PM reaches Swarnadwip to witness joint military exercise
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman reached Swarnadwip in Noakhali on Tuesday to witness a special joint training exercise involving the Army, Navy and Air Force.
The helicopter carrying the prime minister landed on the island at 11:30am, around an hour after he left Dhaka, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony.
Tarique is scheduled to witness the final exercise of "Joint Special Forces Exercise-1-2026", organised for the first time with the participation of special forces from all three services of the Bangladesh Armed Forces.
During the visit, the prime minister will also view a display of military equipment developed using domestic technology and observe various activities of officers and personnel of the three services at the exercise ground.
The Army's Para Commando Brigade, the Navy's SWADS and the Air Force's 501 Air Regiment are taking part in the exercise.
Tarique is scheduled to return to Dhaka by helicopter in the afternoon.

item.title: Owners offer Tk15,800, workers demand Tk22,000 in wage talks
item.description:
The Minimum Wage Board will resume discussions on garment workers' minimum wages at 2pm on Tuesday after failing to reach an agreement between factory owners and workers' representatives over their revised proposals.
The owners have proposed a minimum monthly wage of Tk15,800, while the workers' side has lowered its demand to Tk22,000, leaving a gap of Tk6,200.
At Monday's meeting, held at the board's office in Segunbagicha, Dhaka, both sides revised their earlier proposals. The owners raised their initial offer of Tk15,000 to Tk15,800, while the workers lowered their demand from Tk32,000 to Tk22,000.
Sources familiar with the board said neither side accepted the other's revised proposal.
After the meeting, workers' representative Babul Akhter said the owners' proposal was neither acceptable nor reasonable. He said the workers' side might revise its proposal further after consulting senior labour leaders and expected the owners to come up with a new offer.
Minimum Wage Board Chairman Syed Azad Subhani said discussions were ongoing and information gathered from visits to small, medium and large factories across the country had also been presented.
He said the board was considering inflation, the number of family members dependent on workers, employers' financial capacity, the condition of small and medium-sized factories, and Bangladesh's competitiveness in the international market.
The government formed a six-member Minimum Wage Board on November 1 following protests by garment workers demanding higher wages.
At the board's second meeting on November 9, the workers' side proposed a minimum monthly wage of Tk32,000. The owners' proposal was scheduled to be submitted on November 16, but that meeting was postponed.
Monday's meeting was chaired by board chairman Syed Azad Subhani, with representatives of workers, factory owners and other members present. BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan and Bangladesh Mukto Garment Sramik Union Federation General Secretary Rashedul Alam attended as experts.
Labour unrest continued in industrial areas on Monday despite the ongoing negotiations.
In Gargaria Masterbari area of Sreepur, Gazipur, workers blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway demanding higher wages. Law enforcement personnel dispersed them using sound grenades and tear gas, disrupting traffic.
Production was suspended at around 55 factories in Gazipur amid the unrest.
In Ashulia, authorities declared a holiday at 33 factories on Monday, while another 22 were already closed under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.
Tuesday's meeting is expected to focus on narrowing the gap between the two proposals and reaching an acceptable wage structure.

item.title: Tazreen fire victims still await rehabilitation 14 years on
item.description:
The Tazreen fire remains one of the deadliest industrial disasters in Bangladesh’s garment industry.
On November 24, 2012, a fire at Tazreen Fashions in Nishchintapur, Ashulia, Dhaka, killed 114 workers and injured more than 200.
Marking the 14th anniversary of the tragedy, leaders and activists of various labour organisations held programs to remember those killed and demand rehabilitation for the injured.
More than a decade after the fire, many injured workers have yet to return to normal life. They say most promises of rehabilitation and proper medical treatment remain unfulfilled.
On Tuesday morning, activists of several labour organisations formed a human chain in front of the Tazreen Fashions factory in Nishchintapur, Ashulia. They also paid tribute to the victims by placing flowers at a makeshift memorial.
The fire broke out in a warehouse on the ground floor of the factory on the evening of November 24, 2012, and quickly spread throughout the nine-storey building. Many workers could not escape because the ground-floor exit was locked.
Some workers jumped from the upper floors to escape the flames. Many survived but sustained serious injuries, including fractures to their arms, legs, ribs and hips. Despite years of recovery, many have been unable to resume normal lives.
Official figures show that 114 workers were killed and more than 200 injured in the fire. Labour leaders, however, claim that more than 1,000 workers were injured, including 172 who were permanently disabled. Many are no longer able to work, leaving them struggling to earn a living while dealing with lasting physical injuries.
After the fire, various commitments were made to provide medical treatment, rehabilitation and employment for the injured workers. However, most of these promises have not been fulfilled, labour leaders alleged. Many continue to live in hardship without access to the medical care and rehabilitation they need.
At Tuesday's human chain, labour leaders demanded that the damaged factory building be demolished and replaced with housing for injured workers and a hospital for workers.
They also called for compensation equivalent to the lifetime earnings of each worker killed, proper medical treatment and employment opportunities for injured workers, and the prosecution of the factory owner and others responsible for the fire.
Fourteen years after the Tazreen fire, many injured workers are still struggling to rebuild their lives. Without rehabilitation and employment opportunities, they continue to wait for a chance to return to normal life.

item.title: 112 Bangladeshi workers to fly to Malaysia free of charge on Thursday
item.description:

item.title: Questions linger after Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
item.description:
Jensen Huang's surprise return to Nvidia on Monday appeared to stabilize the US chip giant, along with the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, but questions linger about the long-term impact of his scandal.
An internal investigation overseen by independent directors is still underway at Nvidia regarding concerns that Huang might have been the target of an espionage campaign by China.
US government officials, including President Donald Trump, assured Nvidia's board that reinstating the company's cofounder "poses no national security risk."
In parallel, the US Department of Justice is investigating Megaspeed, a company based in Singapore that allegedly bought processors from Nvidia and routed them to Chinese customers, circumventing US export restrictions.
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has also reportedly launched an investigation into Nvidia's accounting practices and potentially misleading communication to shareholders.
However, the Trump administration has generally avoided going after its allies, so the federal probes might not result in much, Columbia University Professor Eric Talley said.
The embattled chief will nevertheless have to explain himself to lawmakers at a closed-door hearing on December 1 before three House committees.
He will also testify before a Senate committee on December 3 in a hearing that will be livestreamed, while California's attorney general has opened an investigation into the company's chip exports and shareholder disclosures.
There are plenty of regulators who are willing to push back against the Trump administration and ask tough questions, Talley said.
Trump is also known to flip on people whom he no longer considers friends.
"He can become estranged with people, and if that would happen with Jensen Huang, I can imagine a boomerang" on the Trump administration's approach, Talley said.
Openly opposed to Huang's return before ultimately reinstating him, the board is in a delicate position. Former Goldman Sachs chief Lloyd Blankfein predicts its days may be numbered.
A revolt by shareholders, many of whom supported the reinstatement of the 63-year-old entrepreneur, could reshape the board as soon as 2027, since all directors stand for reappointment every year.
If they are spared, the directors could keep Huang on a much "shorter leash" compared to its history of largely deferring to the overwhelming power of this extraordinary executive, Talley said.
"The world is not the same as it was two weeks ago," AI researcher and commentator Gary Marcus wrote on X. "Nvidia is still down a third from what its peak was... (and) reporters are digging around much harder."
Since Huang's resignation, news articles have chipped away at the image of an upbeat, benevolent leader, instead portraying him as a difficult boss and revealing allegations of verbal abuse.
The board's decision "further amplifies the notion that big 'tech bros' don't need to play by the rules like the rest of us do," J. Gold Associates analyst Jack Gold said.
Observers expect a short-term rebound on Wall Street, driven by AI stocks, which began as early as Monday.
AI stocks have fueled the markets over the past two years, but there's still "a lot of noise about financing, geopolitics, durability and skepticism, even though companies across the AI supply chain keep reporting strong demand," Gabelli Funds portfolio manager Hendi Susanto said.

item.title: Actor Sohel Khan dies during film shoot in Bogra
item.description:
Actor Sohel Khan has passed away after suffering a stroke in Bogra on Tuesday morning.
He was taken to the local TMSS Hospital, where doctors declared him dead, reports Prothom Alo.
According to the film's shooting unit, Sohel Khan had been staying in Bogra since November 19 to take part in the film's shooting. His work on the film was scheduled to wrap up on Wednesday.
Members of the shooting unit said he had got ready for the shoot with makeup on Tuesday morning. At one point, a crew member went to call him from his hotel room and found him lying on the bed. When he did not respond, the crew member called out for help, prompting others to rush to the room.
He was then rushed to a private hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

item.title: Work stoppages at 10 Savar garment factories amid wage unrest
item.description:
At least 10 garment factories in Savar saw work stoppages on Tuesday morning as workers continued protests demanding an increase in the minimum wage.
Workers entered all factories that opened in the morning, but employees at the 10 factories stayed away from production as part of their movement to press home their demands.
Superintendent of Police Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan of Industrial Police-1 confirmed the factory closures to Dhaka Tribune on Tuesday morning.
Meanwhile, 20 factories, including Ha-Meem, Envoy and Knit Asia, remain closed indefinitely under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.
No untoward incidents had been reported in the industrial zone by 10am, although law enforcement agencies remained on high alert amid concerns of renewed unrest.
A police official said most workers were unfamiliar with the wage board's procedures, including negotiations and proposals from both employers and workers. Media reports about the employers' wage proposal at Monday's meeting could cause confusion among workers, the official said.
The official also warned that a third party seeking to incite the protests could exploit this lack of awareness, prompting law enforcement agencies to maintain a heightened security presence.

Miss Universe: Mahi says every vote matters in final hours
item.description:
The grand finale of the Miss Universe pageant will take place in Puerto Rico today, Wednesday, 25 November, at 6:00 am Bangladesh time. Contestants are spending busy time rehearsing for the final round. Before that, the preliminary round of the competition was held on 22 November. Contestants presented themselves there in two segments: swimwear and evening gown.

Bangladesh’s representative, Samira Khan Mahi, took part in both segments despite being unwell. Fashion analysts praised her outfits and runway walk in both rounds. Just hours before the grand finale, she had still not fully recovered. Mahi spoke to Prothom Alo’s Hasan Emam via WhatsApp about her physical condition, preparations for the final round and her expectations.

How are you feeling now?

Samira Khan Mahi: I had a fever, along with a sore throat. My blood pressure is also dropping suddenly from time to time. I could not take part in the entire rehearsal session ahead of the final. Even after getting ready, I ultimately had to spend the morning lying in my room. I am feeling somewhat better now and managed to rehearse in the afternoon. However, I cannot speak because of the sore throat. So I am writing my answers to your remaining questions.

Mahi wears khadi sari in Miss Universe, celebrates motherhood and motherland

You had a fever during the preliminary round too, didn’t you?

Samira Khan Mahi: Yes. Only I know how I managed to walk onto the stage taking paracetamol. No one else could understand what I was going through.

People back home are also very hopeful about you.

Samira Khan Mahi: I can see that too. I came here after preparing for such a short time. Even so, the love and votes I have received from people have truly amazed me.

Mahi breaks down in tears after seeing Methila at the camp

Would you like to say anything to your supporters?

Samira Khan Mahi: I would like to express my gratitude to the people of Bangladesh, the people of my country, who have continued to show me love, trust and support. Your love, prayers and votes constantly inspire me. It is a matter of immense pride and emotion for me to represent Bangladesh on such a major international stage.

What are your expectations for the final?

Samira Khan Mahi: I have high expectations for the final. I want to give my very best to represent Bangladesh. I will try to perform in a way that makes people back home proud. Whatever the result, I want Bangladesh’s name to remain in people’s minds.

Miss Universe 2026: Samira Khan Mahi shares behind-the-scenes photos from Puerto Rico

You are currently in second place in the public vote. Do you think you can reach first place?

Samira Khan Mahi: I am keeping track of the voting regularly. The amount of love and response I am receiving from the people of Bangladesh is truly extraordinary. However, the support of people back home will be very important in these final few hours. I would urge everyone to continue voting for me until the very last moment and stand by me. Every single vote is now even more valuable to me. Please keep me in your prayers.

item.title: Ackerman's 150 leads South African onslaught against Bangladesh
item.description:
CRICKET-RSA-BAN-TEST

Marques Ackerman hit a dazzling 150 as South Africa batted themselves into a powerful position on the second day of the second Test against Bangladesh on Tuesday.

Wiaan Mulder also hit a century, making 100 in a South African total of 494 for seven, a massive 403 runs ahead of Bangladesh's first innings total of 91.

Ackerman thrashed his runs off just 138 balls, continuing a remarkable start to his Test career by the 30-year-old left-hander, who has made 470 runs in his first six Test innings, scored at close to a run a ball.

South Africa eye big lead over Bangladesh in 2nd Test

Ackerman was out in unusual circumstances immediately after posting the fastest 150 by a South African in Test cricket. He appeared to lose sight of a full toss from Shoriful Islam and was given out leg before wicket after being struck on the thigh.

Mulder reached his fifth Test century in the last over of the day but was out in the same over, caught behind off part-time spinner Towhid Hridoy.

With only one ball left in the day's play, South Africa indicated that they would probably continue to bat on Wednesday when Simon Harmer went out to join Marco Jansen, who was on 67 not out.

Ackerman has had scores of 6, 95, 62, 157, 0 and 150 since winning his first cap in the second Test against Australia last month.

South Africa beat Bangladesh by 9 wickets in Johannesburg

The slightly-built opening batsman, who used nimble footwork and a wide range of wristy strokes to strike 23 fours and four sixes, became the fourth South African to hit a century before lunch in a Test match, having resumed on his overnight score of 46.

Although there were signs of uneven bounce in the pitch, the Bangladesh bowlers struggled to maintain control and tired towards the end of the day, with Mulder and Marco Jansen putting on 106 for the seventh wicket.

Mulder improved on an impressive conversion rate. It was the sixth time he had reached 50 in a Test and the fifth occasion he went on to make a century.

item.title: RMG wage talks: Workers cut demand to Tk22,000, owners raise offer to Tk15,700
item.description:
RMG workers’ representatives have lowered their minimum wage demand to Tk 22,000 while owners have raised their offer to Tk 15,700 as the Minimum Wage Board continues talks to reach a consensus on a new wage structure.
Both sides are set to submit their third revised wage proposals today, raising hopes of a possible consensus during the ongoing discussions, Wage Board Chairman Syed Azad Subhani said on Tuesday evening.
Briefing reporters at the Minimum Wage Board office at Segunbagicha in the evening Subhani detailed the series of counter-proposals exchanged so far.
He said the owners initially proposed a minimum monthly wage of Tk 15,000 on Monday, to which the workers’ side responded with a revised demand of Tk 25,000.
Owners then raised their offer to Tk 15,500, prompting workers to scale down their demand to Tk 22,000, before the employers finally placed an offer of Tk 15,700, he said.
The third meeting of the government-constituted board resumed on Tuesday afternoon following nearly nine hours of inconclusive discussions held in phases on Monday.
Three expert representatives from the employer and worker sides joined Monday's board meeting for the first time. The employer representatives included Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) President Mahmud Hasan Khan and the association's Senior Additional Secretary Nur Mohammad Amin Rasel.
Rashedul Alam Raju, general secretary of the Bangladesh Mukto Garment Sramik Union Federation, represented the workers.
The agreement marks a breakthrough in the long-running negotiations over workers' demands for higher wages. Details of the new pay structure and its implementation are expected to become clear following the formal announcement.
